text.p: Little change in the weather pattern of Europe continues to mean a strong westerly wind flow through northern and central locations. High winds through the British Isles, English Channel, and North Sea will be hazardous to shipping during the next few days.

Tropical Cyclone 27S, with 40 mph winds, is along the west coast of West Australia near 23s/111e, moving southwest at 10 mph. This system is expected to weaken during the next 48 hours while continuing southwestward and dissipating. Winds will not be a major threat, though heavy rain will spread inland at times over the next several hours before subsiding. The risk of flooding in far western Australia will continue during this time.

Tropical Cyclone Karlette, with 60 mph winds, is in the southwestern Indian Ocean near 27s/57e, moving south southeast at 14 mph. Karlette will continue on a general southeastward track while transitioning into an extratropical weather system. It will become less and less of a threat to shipping as it weakens this period.
